newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close mostly lower.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed mostly lower with rolling of longs and concern over possible exports from Canada yet to come, weighing on the nearby, traders said.
Lumber closed $2.90 per thousand board feet lower to $1.40 higher with March off most at $400.50 and only May up at $390.70 per tbf.
Liquidation continued in March ahead of its spot position next week when trading limits are removed. Many longs again rolled positions into May, traders said.
Although mills are holding asking prices firm, there is concern more wood may become available.

The market remained nervous as the quota year in Canada winds down in March. Mills could still fill 100 percent of the quota before the period ends at the end of March. This would offset some of the expected rise in demand for lumber going in the spring housing market, traders said.
"There was some commercial hedging today," one trader added.
